text:
sarah: seeing a weird oscillation on GPU pools this morning — HPA scaled pods up from our queue-length metric but cluster-autoscaler didn't add nodes, ended up with lots of Pending pods and tail latency spikes

 diego: hmm, logs? CA events?

 sarah: pasted CA events from the nodepool (short):
```
I0318 09:02:11 cluster-autoscaler main.go:... No nodes to scale: NoScaleUpReason: insufficient resources: cpu,gpu
I0318 09:02:12 cluster-autoscaler scale_up.go:... ScaleUp: would add 0 nodes, predicate failed: PodAffinity/Constraints
```

 marta: two likely things: 1) the HPA is driven by an external metric that stales during bursts, so pods are created but not scheduled because they request GPUs; 2) CA expander/scale-up-limit prevented creating GPU nodes quickly.

 kai: can you paste the HPA spec? also wondering if VPA is in recomendation mode and triggering pod restarts that confuse CA/pending counts.

 sarah: HPA spec (redacted):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 40
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: queue_length
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "10"
```

 tina: that external metric (queue_length) is served by our metrics-adapter which caches results for 30s to reduce load. under bursty traffic the adapter returns stale low values for a few cycles and then jumps, so HPA flaps. Also some pods are requesting both gpu and large mem so CA can't find a fit in the warm nodepool.

 diego: pinging infra-bot for CA config & nodepool state

 infra-bot: nodepool-gpu-1: size=6 (max=12), podsPending=23, taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule, unreadyNodes=0, scaleUpInProgress=false

 marta: twofold mitigation: 1) reduce metric cache to 5s for that adapter or use smoothing on HPA (behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds). 2) add a CPU fallback metric so HPA can scale at least to a small baseline before external metric arrives.

 kai: also check cluster-autoscaler --scale-up-delay and max-node-provision-time. we saw in prod that cloud provider provisioning for GPU nodes sometimes takes 4-6m, CA might be throttling scale-ups if its backoff is aggressive.

 sarah: agreed. quick patch I'm going to try: set HPA behavior to reduce downscale aggressiveness and add a second metric entry for cpu utilization (target 40%) so we have hybrid scaling. will also temporarily reduce metrics adapter cache.

 tina: add this guard: use PodTopologySpread and relax strict affinity so CA can binpack GPUs instead of failing predicates. also consider marking the warm preemptible pool as unschedulable for non-gpu pods and allow burst non-preemptible pool for gpu workloads.

 diego: follow-up: do we want CA to respect unschedulable taints and create a separate GPU-only nodepool with taint gpu:true and use tolerations on pods? that reduces predicate failures but we need provision-time trusted.

 marta: yes, make nodepool-gpu-spot for cheap burst, nodepool-gpu-dedicated for stable workload. set CA expander to least-waste and increase maxTotalUnreadyPercentage so CA doesn't stop scaling when many nodes are unready briefly.

 sarah: doing the quick HPA change now. will also post the metric adapter tweak in ops PR. if this works we can schedule a follow-up to tweak VPA mode and CA backoff defaults.

 kai: one more thought — add an external "scale-request" signal to the CA controller via cloudprovider tagging (we did similar for regional warm pools). when HPA needs GPUs urgently, tag to prioritize creation.

 marta: +1, also add observability: per-route queue_length lag metric and CA scale decision traces in console. helps root-cause.

 sarah: thanks everyone, I'll update here after the deploy (expect ~10m). :thumbsup:

 (10m later)
 sarah: patched: HPA now has cpu fallback + behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30, adapter cache 5s. initial results: pending pods dropped from 23 -> 4, new GPU nodes started provisioning, tail p95 down ~320ms -> 85ms. still watching for edge cases.

 diego: great, please make the adapter cache change an opt-in config with a flag and add a note about increased scrape costs.

 marta: filing a follow-up item to review CA backoff & prewarm policies next week.

 sarah: filing ops ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-4321

 kai: nice work.
